newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says even chance of deal with Nats/Lab.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says even chance of deal with Nats/Lab.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday the chances of a coalition deal with the conservative National Party caretaker government or centre-left Labour were still about even.
Entering the latest session of coalition talks, Peters was asked about media speculation that his party was leaning towards National.

"That's the kind of mindless speculation that some of you people indulge in without one shred of substance, and you will keep on doing it till the end of this exercise, and I wish you wouldn't," he said.
Asked it that meant it was still "even stevens" between National and Labour, Peters said: "Yes, that's right."
Peters has been negotiating in parallel with both parties since shortly after the October 12 general election, which left his party holding the balance of power.
Tuesday afternoon's talks with National and Labour are the only formal negotiations scheduled this week, but informal talks are also taking place.
